preApplyRiskProbes.null_body_would_violate_NOT_NULL: 0 in DirectMessage; 0 in eligible Space messages
preApplyRiskProbes.duplicate_messageId_position: 0 - this matters because ConversationMessageMedia also carries a UNIQUE (messageId, position) index that is NOT the ON CONFLICT target, so a duplicate there would ERROR rather than skip
preApplyRiskProbes.system_user_fallback: The Conversation insert COALESCEs to the literal 'system' when a thread has neither participant. No such thread exists (0), and there is no FK on Conversation.startedByUserId, so the fallback is unreachable and harmless here. Flagged because it would write a non-existent user id if it ever fired.
preApplyRiskProbes.directKey_collision: 0 - none of the 5 legacy pairs collides with the 3 existing canonical directKeys. All 5 DirectThreads will migrate WITH pair identity intact.
preApplyRiskProbes.intra_run_directKey_ordering: DirectThreads insert before Spaces, and the CASE re-checks existence at insert time, so a PRIVATE space whose pair was already migrated as a DirectThread would take NULL directKey and keep its history without pair identity. Correct behaviour; named as an outcome to observe rather than a defect.

migrationScriptSafetyAudit.idempotence: Deterministic keys (dt:, sp:, dm:, m:, mm:, dtAs:, dtBs:, sps:) plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING throughout. Re-running inserts zero rows.
migrationScriptSafetyAudit.transactionBehaviour: Statements are issued sequentially without an explicit wrapping transaction. Each INSERT ... SELECT is individually atomic. A mid-run failure therefore leaves earlier statements applied - which is SAFE here only because the script is idempotent and restart-safe: re-running completes the remainder and re-inserts nothing. Stated plainly, because 'it has no transaction' would otherwise read as a defect.
migrationScriptSafetyAudit.paginationAndScale: No pagination - set-based INSERT ... SELECT over 5 threads / 9 messages / 12 spaces / 67 messages / 25 media joins. Trivial at this size.
migrationScriptSafetyAudit.preservation: Reads legacy tables, writes ONLY canonical tables. Media rows are untouched - only the join is re-pointed. Timestamps (createdAt, lastMessageAt, deletedAt), reply chains, dual attribution (actorType/actorInstitutionId to speakingForInstitutionId), read cursors and archive flags all carried.
migrationScriptSafetyAudit.notCarried: Space member ROLES do not survive (parties are plain) - that is the frozen design, not a defect. Named space titles survive as presentation-only Conversation names.
migrationScriptSafetyAudit.failureLogging: Errors propagate and exit non-zero. A run prints MEASUREMENT, then VERIFICATION with migrated-vs-legacy counts, then any SKIPPED spaces, then the grown-past-pair count.
migrationScriptSafetyAudit.dryRunBehaviour: --dry-run prints MEASUREMENT and returns BEFORE any write AND before the verification block. It cannot answer whether the migration has run.
migrationScriptSafetyAudit.defaultBehaviour: No flag means APPLY. There is no confirmation prompt. Worth knowing before anyone runs it casually.

f044.rootCause: `Ready to join` was the presentation for `joinState == idle`, reached as the default branch of the join-state switch. Idle was being read as 'this person has not asked to join', when it also covers 'has asked, and it is in flight' and 'it already finished'. The room issues its join from a POST-FRAME callback, so the first frame paints while the state is still idle — which is why accepting produced a flash of an instruction to accept.

The instruction renders only when the viewer is idle, no join intent is in flight, the session is known-active, and nothing is busy. The screen records join intent SYNCHRONOUSLY in initState (the action is known there; the join is not issued until a frame later), so the first frame already knows the person has asked.
